sections.content:
You know *según* + source from B1 Unit 13 for reporting information. Two more phrases mark where a judgement comes from, or where a statement stops:

• *a juicio de*: "in the opinion of". It is followed by a person or a group whose judgement counts: *a juicio de los expertos*. For yourself, use *a mi juicio* (also *a tu juicio*, *a su juicio*). It presents a judgement that someone could disagree with, not a fact that someone reported.
• *al margen de*: "apart from", "regardless of", "outside". It leaves something aside: *al margen de la política*, *al margen de la ley* (outside the law).

Remember *de* + *el* becomes *del*: *a juicio del director*, *al margen del tema*.

sections.title: Judgement and limits
rows: A juicio de los expertos, el proyecto es demasiado caro.
In the experts' opinion, the project is too expensive.
A mi juicio, el nuevo horario es mejor que el anterior.
In my opinion, the new timetable is better than the old one.
Al margen de las diferencias, los dos amigos se llevan bien.
Differences aside, the two friends get on well.
Trabajaban al margen de la ley.

sections.content: Use *según* for what a source says (a fact, a date, a figure) and *a juicio de* for a judgement (good, bad, too expensive). Both phrases end in *de*, and a person or a noun follows: *a juicio de los expertos*, *al margen de la política*.
